solution:
The correct answer is ​ F = (Meanspace sumspace ofspace squarespace withinspace group)/(Meanspace sumspace ofspace squarespace betweenspace group)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **ANOVA** is used to test the equality of means among more than two groups
 
• The** F-statistic** is the ratio of the mean sum of squares between groups to the mean sum of squares within groups
 
• A larger F-statistic indicates a significant difference in the means among the groups and supports rejection of the null hypothesis
 
• The** critical value** of the F-statistic is determined based on the degrees of freedom and significance level.
 
• In ANOVA, the test statistic F is used to test the null hypothesis that all population means are equal. 
 
 
• F is calculated as the ratio of the mean sum of squares between groups (MSB) to the mean sum of squares within groups (MSW).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] ​ **Additional Information__**

 
• The formula for F is given by:
 
 
• **F = MSB / MSW**
 
 
 
• MSB is the average variance among the group means, and MSW is the average variance within the groups. 
 
• If the null hypothesis is true, then the group means should be similar and the variance within the groups should be larger than the variance between the groups. As a result, the F-statistic should be close to 1.
 
• However, if the null hypothesis is false, and the group means are significantly different, then MSB will be larger than MSW, resulting in a larger F-statistic. 
 
• In such cases, the F-statistic is used to determine the significance of the results, and the null hypothesis is rejected if the F-statistic is larger than the critical value.
